# Benchmarks

```{r model_family_header, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
acousticTS:::.model_family_header(
  family = "psms",
  pages = c(
    Overview = "index.html",
    Theory = "psms-theory.html",
    Implementation = "psms-implementation.html",
    Benchmarks = "psms-benchmarks.html",
    Validation = "psms-validation.html"
  )
)
```

PSMS is benchmarked against the Jech et al. prolate-spheroid cases where tabulated benchmark values exist [@Jech_2015]. The gas-filled benchmark uses the published `140 x 10 mm` broadside geometry and external BEM reference values.

::: {.caution data-title="Precision matters"}
The full liquid-filled branch is the demanding case. Quad precision with the full formulation is the benchmark-close configuration at higher reduced frequency.
:::

|:--|:--|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| `fixed_rigid` | `double` | `FALSE` | `96` | 0.00674 | 0.00230 |
| `fixed_rigid` | `quad` | `FALSE` | `96` | 0.00096 | 0.00083 |
| `pressure_release` | `double` | `FALSE` | `96` | 0.00412 | 0.00251 |
| `pressure_release` | `quad` | `FALSE` | `96` | 0.00433 | 0.00293 |

## Runtime notes

Full liquid-filled quad runs are the slow path because they retain dense overlap-coupled systems. Adaptive mode reduces that cost in quad precision without materially changing the benchmark result on the reported grid.
